title: ATP detection categories and what each toggle covers

checks.do: Which toggle's wording matches the user's symptom, and whether that toggle is set to Block.
Whether the WPAD Protocol toggle exists in the tenant, since no API key is documented for it.

groups.statement: The Advanced Threats Policy tab has ten groups of toggles: Suspicious Content Protection (Page Risk), Botnet Protection, Malicious Active Content Protection, Fraud Protection, Unauthorized Communication Protection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Protection, Suspicious Destinations Protection, P2P File Sharing Protection, P2P Anonymizer Protection and P2P VoIP Protection.

quotes: Suspicious Content Protection (Page RiskTM) - Set the slider
Botnet Protection - Botnets are systems in which attackers
Malicious Active Content Protection - The Zscaler service blocks access
Fraud Protection - Phishing sites are websites that mimic
Unauthorized Communication Protection - Unauthorized communications refer to
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Protection - Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks are a type
Suspicious Destinations Protection - Blocked Countries:
P2P File Sharing Protection - P2P File Sharing refers
P2P Anonymizer Protection - P2P Anonymizer refers
P2P VoIP Protection - P2P VoIP lists several

active-content.statement: Malicious Active Content Protection has four Allow or Block toggles (Malicious Content & Sites for exploit kits, compromised websites and malicious advertising; Vulnerable ActiveX Controls; Browser Exploits; File Format Vulnerabilities for Office and PDF content) plus the Blocked Malicious URLs list.

quotes: Malicious Content & Sites: Choose to Allow or Block websites that attempt to download dangerous content to your browser when you visit them.
Malicious sites include exploit kits, compromised websites, and malicious advertising.
Vulnerable ActiveX Controls: Choose to Allow or Block ActiveX controls that are known to have been exploited.
Browser Exploits: Choose to Allow or Block known web browser vulnerabilities that can be exploited, including exploits for Internet Explorer and Adobe Flash.
File Format Vulnerabilities: Choose to Allow or Block known file format vulnerabilities and suspicious or malicious content in Microsoft Office or PDF documents.

fraud.statement: Fraud Protection has six toggles: Known Phishing Sites, Suspected Phishing Sites (which inspects page content for phishing indications), Spyware Callback, Web Spam, Crypto Mining and Known Adware & Spyware Sites.

quotes: Known Phishing Sites: Choose to Allow or Block websites known to be phishing sites.
Suspected Phishing Sites: Choose to Allow or Block suspected phishing sites. The Zscaler service can inspect the content of a website for indications that it might be a phishing site.
Spyware Callback: Choose to Allow or Block spyware callbacks.
Web Spam: Choose to Allow or Block web pages that pretend to contain useful information
Crypto Mining: Choose to Allow or Block cryptocurrency mining network traffic and scripts.
Known Adware & Spyware Sites: Choose to Allow or Block websites known to contain adware or spyware.

phishing-methods.statement: Phishing detection combines signature-based and AI/ML models and covers URL-based techniques such as typosquatting, punycode, character substitution and domain hijacking.

quotes: Zscaler does this by using a combination of methods to detect various phishing techniques, including signature-based and AI/ML models, and offers protection against URL-based phishing techniques, such as typosquatting, punycode, character substitution, domain hijacking, and many more.

crypto-mining-false-positive.statement: Blocking Crypto Mining can stop sites that use crypto mining as a source of income from working, and can interfere with legitimate attempts to use cryptocurrency for payments.

quotes: However, in some cases, blocking this traffic might cause certain sites that use crypto mining as a source of income to stop working.
It might also interfere with legitimate attempts to use cryptocurrency for payments.

unauthorized-communication.statement: Unauthorized Communication Protection has four toggles: IRC Tunneling and SSH Tunneling (each tunneled over HTTP/S), Anonymizers, and WPAD Protocol, which covers use of the Web Proxy Auto-Discovery protocol from external sources.

quotes: IRC Tunneling: Choose to Allow or Block IRC traffic being tunneled over HTTP/S.
SSH Tunneling: Choose to Allow or Block. This refers to SSH traffic being tunneled over HTTP/S.
Anonymizers: Choose to Allow or Block applications and methods used to obscure the destination and the content accessed by the user.
WPAD Protocol: Choose to Allow or Block the use of the Web Proxy Auto-Discovery (WPAD) protocol from external sources

xss.statement: XSS protection has two toggles: Cookie Stealing, for third-party sites that gather cookie information (often IPS signature-based and so high fidelity), and Potentially Malicious Requests, a type of cross-site scripting request.

quotes: Cookie Stealing: Choose to Allow or Block third-party websites that gather cookie information
These detections are often IPS signature-based detections, so they are high fidelity.
Potentially Malicious Requests: These are a type of cross-site scripting request. Select Block to block cross-site scripting.

bittorrent-uninspectable.statement: BitTorrent can be allowed or blocked, but its content is encrypted and cannot be inspected.

quotes: BitTorrent: Choose to Allow or Block the usage of BitTorrent, a popular P2P file sharing application. Content downloaded with BitTorrent is encrypted, and therefore it cannot be inspected.

hangouts-deprecated.statement: Google Hangouts is deprecated and replaced by Google Chat; controls for Google Chat and other cloud applications are in Cloud App Control, in an Instant Messaging rule.

quotes: Google Hangouts has been deprecated by Google and replaced by Google Chat.
select an Instant Messaging Rule to edit.

capture-on-block.statement: If Traffic Capture is enabled, the Capture option appears when Block is selected, unlike Malware Protection where it appears for Allow or Block. Capturing Allow and Block traffic for web and non-web threat categories is done in the IPS Control policy.

quotes: If Traffic Capture is enabled, the Capture option appears when Block is selected.
To capture web and non-web threat category traffic with the Allow and Block actions, see Configuring the IPS Control Policy.

toggle-wire-keys.statement: The console toggles map to these settings keys: Malicious Content & Sites = malwareSitesBlocked; Vulnerable ActiveX Controls = activeXBlocked; Browser Exploits = browserExploitsBlocked; File Format Vulnerabilities = fileFormatVunerabilitesBlocked; Known Phishing Sites = knownPhishingSitesBlocked; Suspected Phishing Sites = suspectedPhishingSitesBlocked; Spyware Callback = suspectAdwareSpywareSitesBlocked; Web Spam = webspamBlocked; Crypto Mining = cryptoMiningBlocked; Known Adware & Spyware Sites = adSpywareSitesBlocked; IRC Tunneling = ircTunnellingBlocked; SSH Tunneling = sshTunnellingBlocked; Anonymizers = anonymizerBlocked; Cookie Stealing = cookieStealingBlocked; Potentially Malicious Requests = potentialMaliciousRequestsBlocked; BitTorrent = bitTorrentBlocked; Tor = torBlocked; Google Hangouts = googleTalkBlocked; Command & Control Servers = cmdCtlServerBlocked; Command & Control Traffic = cmdCtlTrafficBlocked; Domain Generation Algorithm (DGA) Domains = dgaDomainsBlocked. Each is a boolean; the Capture flag is the same key with the Capture suffix, except cookie stealing.
toggle-wire-keys.conditions: The mapping rests on each key's API description matching the help page's wording (for example suspectAdwareSpywareSitesBlocked describes spyware callback traffic and googleTalkBlocked names Google Hangouts). No source lists the pairs.

wpad-no-key.statement: No WPAD key appears in the OpenAPI ATP settings object, although the console has a WPAD Protocol toggle.
wpad-no-key.conditions: An absence: the spec lists 48 properties and none names WPAD. The SDKs mirror the spec. A toggle that exists only in the console cannot be read or written by the API.

wpad-api.title: How the WPAD Protocol toggle is represented in the API
wpad-api.detail: The help page documents a WPAD Protocol toggle; no ATP settings key in the OpenAPI document or either SDK names it. Whether it is stored under another key, omitted from the API, or not present in all tenants is not shown.
